claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
A portion of Hf and Ta can be substituted with lighter elements such as Nb or V.
Nb and V are lighter substitution elements relative to Hf and Ta.
Substitution of Hf and Ta with Nb or V will reduce the alloy's average atomic mass.
The proposed substitution will reduce the density of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified alloy will maintain or slightly improve its room-temperature strength and hardness.
The modified alloy will maintain or slightly improve its elevated-temperature strength and hardness, including at approximately 1000 °C.
The substitution may maintain or slightly alter solid-solution strengthening.
The substitution may maintain or slightly alter high-temperature stability mechanisms.
The proposed intervention is applicable from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The applicable loading conditions are assumed to fall within unspecified standard operational limits.
The density reduction and mechanical-property response depend on substitution identity, substitution proportion, and resulting microstructure.
Alloys with varying lighter-element substitution levels should be compared with as-cast HfMoTaTiZr by density, tensile-strength, and hardness measurements at room temperature and 1000 °C.
The stated rejection rule requires both less than 5% density reduction and failure to maintain mechanical properties within 10% of baseline values.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires both reduced density and preserved mechanical properties, so failure of either requirement should reject it. The stated rule instead uses a conjunction, requiring both inadequate density reduction and inadequate property retention; it would not reject an alloy that fails only one of the two core requirements.
